question: *** Did William John Taylor go to sea? ***
what was found: *** 1891 census, his father's household at 2 Fore Street, Northam: 'William J TAYLOR, Son, Single, 20, born Bideford - CAB DRIVER'. *** His father, William Taylor, 65, is *** 'Cab driver, retired sergeant, cavalry'. ***
verdict: *** NO. HE FOLLOWED HIS FATHER'S TRADE. *** At twenty he is driving a cab in Northam, which is precisely the age at which a seafaring career would already have begun. *** The ADM 188 null now has a reason behind it: he is not in the Royal Navy registers because he was not a seaman at all. ***

question: *** Did Horace Archibald Taylor go to sea? ***
what was found: *** The same return: 'Horace A TAYLOR, Son, 19 - FOOTMAN, DOMESTIC SERVANT'. ***
verdict: *** NO. *** In domestic service at nineteen. *** Two brothers, two land trades, on one census page. ***

question: *** So what would the crew-list search have cost? ***
what was found: Crew lists are arranged by the ship's *** official number ***, not by name, so a man can only be found once his ship is known. For Bideford, Barnstaple and Appledore registry that is on the order of *** a hundred-odd vessels across twenty-five years ***, each with an annual agreement - *** several thousand documents ***, held in three places at once (TNA, the National Maritime Museum, and the Maritime History Archive in Newfoundland).
verdict: *** Days of work, across three institutions, for a question the census answers in one line. *** Written down so that nobody reopens it as though it were merely untried.

question: *** And it could not have been done by name anyway ***
what was found: The name-indexed registers of merchant seamen cover *** 1835-1857 *** and then resume with the Central Index Register of *** 1918-1941. *** Between them there is *** no surviving central register of seamen. ***
verdict: *** The two men's whole working lives fall inside that gap. *** Even with unlimited hours there is *** no index that converts a name into a ship *** for the years 1885 to 1910, which is when either of them would have sailed. *** The route was never available, quite apart from being unnecessary. ***

question: *** What is left of the seafaring question ***
verdict: *** Closed for these two men, and only for them. *** The Taylors of *** Appledore *** on the *** Ulelia *** - T Taylor mate b.1846, J W Taylor master b.1888, T G Taylor b.1893 - are still *** joined to this family by nothing at all ***, and this finding does not touch them. *** If anything it widens the gap: *** a cab-driving, footmanning household in Northam looks less like a branch of a shipmaster's family, not more. *** Still not asserted either way. ***
